contract.note: The Gemini launch comparison is reasonable. However, requiring that no frontier release made a large jump converts an overall characterization of progress into a universal claim. One large benchmark jump does not establish exponential progress over 18 months.

evidence.note: Google confirms the launch model and direction of benchmark improvements, but gives no magnitudes. Its speed and modality disclosures concern additional dimensions outside the contract's benchmark comparison.
The reproduced MMLU-Pro scores support a modest improvement over 1.5 Pro on this measure. They do not establish modest gains across all capabilities or verify the source's 34.3 figure.
The reproduced 11-point HiddenMath gain challenges the characterization of the Gemini improvement as tiny. It does not establish large gains on most benchmarks.

OpenAI's disclosed reasoning gains challenge the broad characterization of recent results as incremental. These company results do not independently establish an exponential trend or prove the contract's universal interpretation fair.

reviews.rationale: The frozen contract strengthens a general trend description into a claim that no large jump occurred. Gemini gains vary by benchmark, and o1 supplies meaningful counterevidence, but a single jump cannot resolve incremental versus exponential progress. Scoring under this contract would depend on an unfair added quantifier.
